title: Google Gemini Adds Direct Editing for PDFs, Docs, Sheets and More
content:
Google has announced that users can now generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Gemini. These new file editing capabilities are available to all Gemini users starting today. While PDF previews and editing are supported on both web and mobile platforms, all other file formats are currently available only in the web version.

This update builds on earlier support for generating and downloading files, allowing users to modify documents without leaving the Gemini app. Google stated that users can expand documents to edit them in full-screen mode and highlight text within files to ask questions or provide prompts.
summary: Google Gemini now lets users generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown, TXT, and code directly within the app. The new file editing features are available to all Gemini users today, with PDF editing working on both web and mobile, while other formats are limited to the web version.
author: The Verge

title: GM to pay $220 million to settle data sales claims
content:
General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to resolve claims that it illegally sold driver and location information to data brokers. This settlement addresses a complaint filed by a coalition of 36 US attorneys general. Under the agreement, GM is required to limit the driving data it collects and must obtain "express consent" from drivers before gathering their information.

The allegations center on GM’s now-discontinued Smart Driver program, which collected data regarding driving habits such as acceleration, braking, and trip length. The company allegedly shared this information with data brokers, which enabled insurance companies to purchase the data.
summary: General Motors agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold driver and location data to data brokers. The settlement, prompted by a complaint from 36 US attorneys general, requires GM to limit data collection and obtain express consent from drivers.
author: The Verge

title: Rivian R2 becomes best-selling vehicle as Q3 revenue rises 38%
content:
Rivian’s R2 has become the company’s best-selling vehicle, outselling all other electric models for the first time. This milestone was highlighted as Rivian reported its third-quarter 2026 earnings, a period marked by ramping up production of the R2. The company noted that the R2 is now leading sales across its entire electric vehicle lineup.

Financially, Rivian generated $2.155 billion in total revenue, a 38 percent increase from $1.558 billion in the same quarter of 2025. Automotive revenue accounted for $1.55 billion, rising 36 percent year over year, while software and subscription services contributed $605 million, reflecting a 45 percent annual growth.
summary: Rivian reported $2.155 billion in third-quarter revenue, a 38 percent increase from the same period in 2025. The R2 electric vehicle is now outselling all other Rivian models for the first time.
author: The Verge

title: Google says AI search earns less than organic, plans more ads to boost revenue
content:
Alphabet reported its third-quarter financial results on Wednesday, revealing nearly $128 billion in revenue and over $26 billion in net income for the July-to-September period. Despite a 25 percent year-over-year revenue increase, the company’s stock price fell by almost 12 percent, marking one of its largest post-earnings drops in history. The market reaction was driven by earnings per share of $2.12, which fell short of the consensus projection of $3.02, and a net income figure that was approximately $9 billion lower than the previous year.

A key factor in the stock’s decline was Google’s admission that its AI search feature generates less revenue than traditional organic search. This revelation is particularly notable given that the company expects to increase its spending on AI in the coming year. Although Google’s Cloud division exceeded expectations with revenue surpassing $30 billion—roughly $1 billion more than analyst estimates—the overall financial performance failed to satisfy investors. The combination of lower-than-expected profitability and rising AI costs contributed to the significant drop in the company’s share price.
summary: Alphabet posted Q3 2026 revenue of almost $128 billion and net income of $26 billion, but said AI search earns less than organic search. The company’s shares fell about 12 % after the report, and it plans to spend more on AI and add ads to raise revenue.
author: Ars Technica

title: Small company offers concentrated solar system with integrated fossil fuel backup
content:
Concentrated solar energy, which uses mirrors to convert sunlight into heat for driving turbines, initially appeared to have a promising future due to advancements in heat storage that allowed for around-the-clock power generation. However, the technology failed to maintain its competitive edge as the cost of photovoltaic panels dropped significantly, making solar panels the cheapest power source in most locations. Consequently, current solar power generation requires a mix of other facilities, typically batteries and natural gas plants, to manage overnight demands and weather-related shortfalls.

A small company is now offering a solution that aims to eliminate the need for constructing separate backup facilities. Its concentrated solar design integrates a fossil-fueled backup system that shares most of its generating hardware with the solar component. This approach allows the system to function as its own backup, potentially reducing the infrastructure required to ensure continuous power supply.
summary: A small company is promising to reduce the need for separate battery or natural gas facilities by creating a concentrated solar system. Its design allows a fossil-fueled backup system to share most of the generating hardware with the solar side.
author: Ars Technica

title: Trump Declares Foreign-Made Robot Imports a National Security Threat
content:
President Donald Trump issued a presidential proclamation on October 28 declaring that imports of foreign‑made factory robots pose a national security threat. The proclamation orders new negotiations with U.S. trading partners and leaves open the possibility of future tariffs on such robot imports.

The measure heightens scrutiny of foreign‑made industrial robots that could complicate the manufacturing operations of major U.S. companies that rely on them. Trump singled out Detroit automakers General Motors and Ford, electric‑vehicle maker Tesla, and aerospace and defense giants Boeing and Lockheed Martin as examples of firms that could be affected.

In the proclamation, Trump described industrial robots and machinery as essential for producing U.S. military weapon systems and as a “driving force” behind all critical infrastructure sectors of the U.S. economy.

The proclamation cites an investigation conducted under U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, which found that U.S. imports of such robots “pose[] risks to the United States industrial base and threatens the long‑term competitiveness of the United States in a sector that is increasingly vital to national security.”
summary: Trump Declares Foreign-Made Robot Imports a National Security Threat.
author: Ars Technica

title: Pentagon IG declines to investigate Starlink/Starshield slowdown in Ukraine
content:
The Pentagon inspector‑general’s office has declined a request from U.S. senators to investigate recent restrictions on Ukraine’s use of SpaceX’s satellite services. The inquiry, directed at the Department of Defense inspector general Platte Moring, came after Ukraine reported that its military drones lost satellite connectivity when flying faster than 161 km per hour (100 mph). The Ukrainian military said the speed limit was lifted after roughly ten days.

Five Democratic and four Republican senators sent an October 15 letter to Moring asking for a probe into the reported disruptions of both Starlink and its military‑grade counterpart, Starshield. The letter sought answers on whether any restrictions were directed, authorized, or implemented by SpaceX, the Department of Defense, or other U.S. government entities; whether such restrictions complied with applicable U.S. government contracts; and what actions, if any, the Department of Defense took in response.

The inspector‑general’s office has refused to open an investigation into the matter.
summary: Pentagon IG declines to investigate Starlink/Starshield slowdown in Ukraine.
author: Ars Technica

title: Windows 11 preview update fixes right‑click menu, amid declining PC license sales
content:
Microsoft has begun rolling out a Windows 11 preview update, KB5127936, that addresses a long‑standing complaint from power users about the operating system’s right‑click menu. The update, which is cumulative for Windows 11 versions 26H2 and 25H2, will be delivered gradually before moving to a normal rollout for all devices once it reaches general availability.

The new preview introduces a “customize menu” button that lets users control which commands appear when they right‑click. Built‑in items such as Send To or Create Shortcut can be toggled on or off, the order of main‑menu items can be rearranged, and third‑party extensions can be assigned to either the main menu or the “Show more options” submenu. The change is intended to restore the muscle memory that many users had lost when familiar commands were hidden behind icons or moved to a submenu.

Alongside the menu overhaul, the preview highlights a new feature called Cloud Rebuild. This recovery option can reinstall Windows 11 directly from the cloud when the current installation fails to boot. The process pulls the Windows 11 image and required system drivers from Windows Update, eliminating the need for a custom recovery image or external media. Cloud Rebuild behaves more like a fresh installation than a repair, as existing applications and files are not retained; users can also choose to sanitize entire system drives before reinstalling.

The announcement comes at the same time Microsoft released its quarterly financial report, which noted a continued decline in the business of selling Windows licenses for new PCs. For a complete list of improvements included in the preview—such as changes to Xbox mode and settings—see the official Microsoft release announcement.
summary: The preview update KB5127936 for Windows 11 26H2 and 25H2 adds a customizable right‑click menu that lets users toggle, rearrange, and control built‑in and third‑party commands. It also introduces Cloud Rebuild, a recovery option that reinstalls Windows 11 from the cloud without external media but does not preserve existing applications or files.
author: Ars Technica

title: Granola Adds Dictation to Meeting Notetaker to Compete with Wispr
content: Wispr recently expanded its dictation app to include meeting notes. In response, Granola is adding dictation functionality to its meeting‑notetaking tool. The move signals a growing competition in the voice‑AI space.
summary: After Wispr added meeting notes to its dictation app, Granola is adding dictation to its meeting notetaker. The voice AI wars are getting interesting.
author: TechCrunch

title: Meta launches AI fashion app Style Sketch
content: Meta has quietly launched an AI‑driven fashion app called Style Sketch. The app links to Instagram to automatically create a virtual closet from photos users have already posted. It also allows users to add items manually by snapping a photo, recording a short video, or uploading images from their camera roll.
summary: Meta has launched an AI fashion app called Style Sketch. The app connects to Instagram to build a virtual closet from shared photos and lets users add items by snapping a photo, recording a video, or uploading images from their camera roll.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI Agents Replace Human Roles at Startup Anything
content: Using AI for roles from executive assistants to chiefs of staff, companies are boasting about doing more with less, creating tension with their human workers On an average workday, Dhruv Amin chats with dozens of colleagues to get things done at his AI startup Anything. He might ask Gwen, his executive assistant, to schedule a meeting, then troubleshoot a technical problem with Cody, his coding partner. Then he might check in with Betsy for search engine optimization, or Juno for onboarding customers. If the office runs out of snacks, he sends a Slack message to Justin, the office manager charged with stocking the kitchen. But none of these co-workers are people. They’re artificial intelligence agents, software that handles tasks without human intervention. Anything is one of several startups building them, and betting on a future where workplaces will increasingly turn over their sales, marketing, coding and other tasks to semi-autonomous AI. At Anything, there are 15 human employees and roughly 150 agents – a ratio that Amin believes will soon be the norm.
summary: Dhruv Amin, founder of AI startup Anything, uses AI agents named Gwen, Cody, Betsy, Juno, and Justin to handle tasks such as scheduling, coding, SEO, onboarding, and snack stocking. The company has 15 human employees and about 150 AI agents, a ratio Amin believes will become common.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Vatican Displays Eight Historic Popemobiles Tracing Century-Long Papal Transport
content: Eight historic popemobiles are now on display at the Vatican Museums, showcasing the evolution of papal transport over nearly a century. The exhibition features a range of vehicles, from silk‑lined limousines to models equipped with bulletproof glass, illustrating how papal transport has changed through the ages.
summary: Eight historic popemobiles, ranging from silk-lined limousines to vehicles fitted with bulletproof glass, are on display at the Vatican Museums. The exhibition traces how papal transport has evolved over nearly a century.
author: Euronews

title: Kazakhstan President Tokayev urges faster construction of nuclear power plants
content: President Tokayev delivered his annual address, outlining Kazakhstan’s priorities for the coming year. He urged the government to accelerate energy and construction projects, specifically calling for faster construction of nuclear power plants. Tokayev also criticized inefficiencies in public policy, urging reforms to improve overall project execution.
summary: President Tokayev said the country should speed up construction of nuclear power plants. In his annual address he outlined priorities for the coming year, urging faster energy and construction projects and criticizing inefficiencies in public policy.
author: Euronews

title: Spain high‑speed train crash expert calls blaming human error absurd
content: Following Spain's deadly high-speed train crash, Delano D'Souza is joined by Francisco Badea, Director of FEM Expert Engineering, Railway Structural & PRM Certification Expert. Batea challenges explanations that reduce railway disasters to isolated human mistakes. “It is basically an absurdity to say that it depended on one person and one human mistake,” he argues, emphasizing that modern railway networks operate through multiple layers of protection, including automated safeguards, train-detection technologies, operational protocols and institutional oversight. “The system has been designed in a way that this type of accident should never happen.”
summary: Spain's deadly high‑speed train crash was described as an accident that should never have happened. Francisco Badea, Director of FEM Expert Engineering, said it is absurd to attribute the crash to a single human mistake because modern railway systems have multiple layers of protection, including automated safeguards, train‑detection technologies, operational protocols and institutional oversight.
author: France 24

title: Retired Lt. Gen. Ben Hodges says Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is removing dissenting officers
content:
Erin Ogunkeye welcomed Lt. General (ret.) Ben Hodges, the former commander of U.S. Army Europe and NATO Allied Land Command, to discuss recent concerns about the treatment of senior military leaders.  

Hodges highlighted the dismissal of Lt. General Brett Sylvia, arguing it signals a troubling pattern within the Pentagon under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. He criticized the reluctance of retired senior commanders to speak publicly against policies they view as damaging, saying he was “disappointed and surprised” by the limited public resistance among former four‑star generals.
summary: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Lt. General (ret.) Ben Hodges, former commander of US Army Europe and NATO Allied Land Command.
author: France 24

title: French government proposes bill forcing protesters to pay up to €10,000 for riot damage
content: France is working to recover after riots and looting erupted on the periphery of nationwide peaceful demonstrations on October 17. In the aftermath, the government is advancing legislation that would require protesters to pay reparations of up to €10,000 for damage caused during public unrest, regardless of whether they were directly responsible for the vandalism. The proposed bill targets financial liability for participants in demonstrations linked to the recent disturbances.
summary: The French government is advancing a bill that would require protesters to pay reparations for damage caused during public unrest. The legislation would set liability at up to €10,000 per protester even if they were not directly responsible for the vandalism.
author: France 24

title: Paris suburb shooting suspect says he targeted Muslims, Africans
content: A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week has told prosecutors that he deliberately targeted individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African or North African. The assault left one person dead and injured seven others, including a child. Prosecutors disclosed the suspect’s admission on Thursday. The incident occurred as the political climate in France grows increasingly tense, with the country about six months away from the next spring presidential election.
summary: A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week has admitted to targeting individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African, prosecutors said on Thursday. The attack killed one person and wounded seven others, including a child.
author: France 24

title: Republicans target Michigan candidate El‑Sayed in midterm race
content: What in the name of political free speech is off-limits? Can you say whatever you want on the campaign trail, no matter how false or racist?
summary: Michigan's El‑Sayed is being targeted by Republicans in the midterms race. The article raises questions about the limits of political free speech on the campaign trail.
author: France 24

title: Paris suburb shooting underscores rising far‑right extremist threat in France
content:
François Picard welcomed Dr Joseph Downing, a Senior Lecturer in International Relations and Politics at Aston University, to discuss the rise of extremist right‑wing ideologies in France and elsewhere in the democratic world.  

Downing noted that France’s politics of insecurity now extends beyond crime to issues of national identity, the disappearance of a political centre and the erosion of democratic values. He linked the emergence of far‑right extremist violence and the ongoing stigmatization of ethnically diverse working‑class suburbs to a recent deadly shooting in the Paris suburbs, which he said was allegedly motivated by racist and anti‑Muslim hostility.
summary: Paris suburb shooting underscores rising far‑right extremist threat in France.
author: France 24

title: Star Trek and X‑Men star Patrick Stewart dies at 86
content: British actor Patrick Stewart died at age 86, a statement released on Thursday announced. Stewart, an acclaimed performer with the Royal Shakespeare Company, later starred in the 1980s sci‑fi television series “Star Trek” and subsequently appeared in the “X‑Men” franchise.
summary: British actor Patrick Stewart has died at age 86, a statement released on Thursday said. He was an acclaimed Royal Shakespeare Company performer who later starred in the TV series Star Trek and the X‑Men franchise.
author: France 24

title: China leaders call for greater loyalty and initiative at CCP session
content: At a recent Chinese Communist Party session, leaders called for greater loyalty and initiative while stressing internal discipline. The meeting did not resolve the question of Xi Jinping’s successor, and party officials expressed concern about potential instability as geopolitical tensions rise and the Chinese economy shows signs of cooling.
summary: The CCP session emphasized internal discipline — as expected, but left the question of Xi Jinping's successor unanswered. The party seems anxious of any instability as geopolitics heats up and China's economy cools down.
author: DW World

title: India finance ministry raises fiscal-year growth forecast, warns of fuel inflation
content: India’s Ministry of Finance has raised its growth forecast for the current fiscal year. At the same time, the ministry cautioned that inflation could remain a concern, especially for fuel and energy prices, given ongoing instability in the Middle East.
summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. It warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.
author: DW World

title: Russian drone attack on Dnipro railway station kills 13 civilians
content: The United Nations’ top humanitarian official in Ukraine condemned a Russian drone attack on Dnipro’s main railway station on Thursday. The strike killed at least 13 civilians and injured 10 others.
summary: On Thursday, the UN’s top humanitarian official in Ukraine condemned a Russian drone attack on Dnipro’s main railway station. The strike killed at least 13 civilians and injured 10 others.
author: UN News

title: Qatar calls accusations of election interference in Israel “ridiculous and dangerous”
content: Netanyahu’s claim of interference in election also dismissed by Israeli police and opposition parties Israel’s choice: Netanyahu remaining in power or a Palestinian-backed coalition Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party and Benjamin Netanyahu’s main rival, has warned political opponents against exploiting allegations of foreign interference in Israel’s election to delay the swearing-in of the next Knesset. In remarks posted on X, Eisenkot said: Israel must safeguard the integrity of the elections against any attempt at interference, spin and manipulation, and examine every complaint thoroughly. On the other hand, political actors must not be allowed to exploit the situation and affect the swearing-in date of the 26th Knesset.”
summary: Qatar calls accusations of election interference in Israel “ridiculous and dangerous”.
author: Guardian World

title: US Vice President JD Vance sends diplomatic letter to Iran's Mohsen Rezaei
content:
US Vice President JD Vance has sent a personal letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s supreme national security council, in an effort to restart diplomacy and avert a major new conflict between the two nations. The correspondence, which arrived on Sunday following predominantly Qatari mediation, signals that Washington has not abandoned diplomatic channels ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.

The letter proposes a specific framework for negotiations, requiring Tehran to agree to commitments on its nuclear program at the outset of the process. In exchange for these initial steps, the US would provide sanctions relief, with the aim of opening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days.
summary: US Vice President JD Vance wrote a personal letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s supreme national security council, after predominantly Qatari mediation. The letter asks Tehran to make nuclear‑program commitments that would open the Strait of Hormuz within seven days in exchange for US sanctions relief.
author: Guardian World

title: German actress Elke Sommer dies at 85 in Los Angeles
content:
German actress Elke Sommer, known for her work in “A Shot in the Dark,” the early‑1970s Agatha Christie adaptation “And Then There Were None,” and the British comedy “Carry on Behind,” has died at age 85. Bild magazine reported that she passed away in Los Angeles from heart failure.

Born in Berlin, Sommer’s facility with languages helped her transition from European cinema to Hollywood, where she appeared alongside actors such as Peter Sellers, Dick Van Dyke and Paul Newman. Her career peaked in the 1960s and 1970s, making her one of the few German performers of that era to achieve notable success in English‑language films and to be highlighted for her bombshell image.
summary: Elke Sommer, the Berlin-born German star of "A Shot in the Dark", "And Then There Were None" and "Carry on Behind", died at age 85. Bild magazine reported she died in Los Angeles of heart failure.
author: Guardian World

title: Seven tankers with 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel head to US
content:
Seven oil tankers carrying an estimated 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel are sailing towards the US, according to tracking data from Greenpeace. This shipment represents the first phase of a supply deal negotiated between presidents Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin earlier this month, which reverses years of sanctions on Russian oil.

Uncertainty remains regarding whether the vessels will be able to unload their cargo, as a political dispute continues over the legality of the shipments.
summary: Seven tankers with 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel head to US.
author: Guardian World

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang targeted by Chinese spy linked to Megaspeed executive
content:
U.S. intelligence agencies say Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has been targeted by a Chinese spy, according to a New York Times report. The alleged spy, identified as Alice Huang—or Huang Le—is an executive at Singapore‑based datacenter firm Megaspeed and is not related to the Nvidia CEO.  

Officials previously suspected her of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, prompting surveillance. Unnamed sources cited by the newspaper say the agencies have concluded she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information about Nvidia to Beijing.
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang targeted by Chinese spy linked to Megaspeed executive.
author: Guardian World

title: Hong Kong leader apologises for residential fire that killed 168 people
content:
Hong Kong’s deadliest residential fire since 1980 killed 168 people, and survivors and bereaved families have said justice has yet to be served.  

In a rare public act of contrition, Chief Executive John Lee apologized for government shortcomings that contributed to the blaze. Lee and seven other officials bowed in apology at the release of a report that identified “decades of failure” by government bodies. The apology, however, did not satisfy many victims’ families.
summary: Hong Kong chief executive John Lee and seven other officials apologized for government shortcomings that contributed to the fire that killed 168 people last year. The apology was made when a report citing “decades of failure” by government bodies was released, though some survivors and families said justice remains unmet.
author: Guardian World

title: Lula’s runoff victory trounces far right, hailed as win for planet and democracy
content: The trouncing of the far right provides a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France Thank you, Brazil, for demonstrating how the far right can be trounced while protection for the Amazon is strengthened. In a world where nature and democracy appeared to be bleeding out in tandem, voters and forest defenders in this global south powerhouse have shown it is possible to staunch the flow. This should provide much needed inspiration and, more practically, a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France. The astonishing comeback victory of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Sunday’s presidential runoff against his extreme right challenger Flavío Bolsonaro has brought oceans of rapturous supporters on to the streets, while also thrilling conservationists, climate activists and social justice campaigners across the world.
summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil’s presidential runoff on Sunday, defeating far‑right challenger Flavío Bolsonaro. The victory was celebrated by supporters, conservationists and climate activists as a model for social and environmental movements in other elections such as those in the US, Spain and France.
author: Guardian World

title: Bryan Adams releases new song “Lake Ontario” criticizing Donald Trump
content: Musician wrote a ‘love letter’ to Canada with a new album – and some pointed commentary about the US president Lake Ontario, the vast body of water that straddles the US-Canada border, has gone by many names over the centuries: Lac Saint-Louis, Lacus Ontarius, Skaniadorio, Cataraqui Lake. But one thing it will never be called, says the Canadian rock star Bryan Adams, is Lake America. In his new song Lake Ontario, Adams takes aim at the US president, Donald Trump, accusing him of “breaking the peace” between the people who live on the lake’s shores. The ‘lake of shining waters ’ is what the Iroquois called her It’s a First Nations name – not an executive order. But things weren’t going his way in Iran So like a baby tossing the toys from the pram You can push us to the brink But where the open road divides
summary: Bryan Adams releases new song “Lake Ontario” criticizing Donald Trump.
author: Guardian World

title: SpaceX Starfall capsule delivers Air Force cargo in point-to-point test
content:
The U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) confirmed the successful recovery of cargo pods from SpaceX’s Starfall capsule, marking a significant milestone in testing point-to-point rocket cargo delivery. The AFRL announced via social media on October 26 that the agile cargo pods were recovered after splashdown in the Pacific Ocean. This mission utilized the secretive, uncrewed reentry vehicle to transport military equipment through space and back to Earth, demonstrating the potential for rapid global mobility for the Future Force.

The Starfall capsule launched on a Falcon 9 rocket as part of SpaceX’s Bandwagon-5 mission, which lifted off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on October 20. AFRL Technology Transition Office director Adam Remaly described the event as a critical achievement in examining the viability of Rocket Cargo delivery. The mission involved a series of AFRL-developed cargo pods designed to carry various items, including medical equipment, food ration packs, and other military kit intended for emergencies in locations difficult to reach via conventional transportation.

Each cargo pod contained sensors to monitor temperature conditions and measure shock and vibration forces exerted on the cargo during launch, reentry, and splashdown. Researchers specifically monitored electronics and survival gear, which included a SATCOM-enabled tracker, batteries, a reverse osmosis desalinator, and emergency medical equipment. Additionally, the AFRL conducted a fit check of a UNI-PAC III life raft inside the Starfall capsule, a component that could potentially be included in future tests.

SpaceX’s disk-shaped Starfall capsule made its debut on a Falcon 9 launch in June, with the company maintaining relative silence about the vehicle. According to a Federal Aviation Administration environmental assessment published earlier this year, the hockey-puck-shaped vehicle measures approximately 3.1 meters (10.2 feet) across. It is capable of returning up to 1,000 kilograms (2,200 pounds) of cargo from orbit and features a carbon fiber heat shield, compressed gas thrusters for attitude control, and a parachute system for precision landings.

The AFRL will now assess the data recovered from the October 20 mission to support its broader Rocket Cargo initiative. The Air Force aims to evolve this program to transport tens of tons of cargo per launch, a capacity that exceeds Starfall’s current limits. While SpaceX’s larger Starship rocket was a likely candidate for tests at Johnston Atoll, those plans were suspended in July 2025 due to environmental concerns, leaving the status of the search for an alternative site unclear.
summary: The Air Force Research Laboratory recovered SpaceX's Starfall cargo capsule in the Pacific Ocean after it launched on a Falcon 9 rocket on October 20. The mission tested AFRL-developed pods carrying military equipment to assess the viability of point-to-point rocket cargo delivery.
author: Space.com

title: Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope reflects stars at La Silla Observatory
content: The Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope reflects the stars at the La Silla Observatory in Chile. (Image credit: J. Rodrigues/ESO) Stars shine in the vast aluminum dish of the Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope (SEST) in this photograph captured by astronomer and astrophotographer José Rodrigues during a recent visit to the European Southern Observatory's La Silla Observatory in Chile. What is it? Rodrigues' image captures "airglow" infusing the night sky over La Silla with a soft orange glow, which is created as sunlight interacts with molecules in the upper atmosphere, according to the University of Lancaster. The subtle phenomenon can be seen reflected in the 15-meter (49-foot) primary dish of the SEST telescope along with the myriad stars of the Southern Hemisphere, as the dome of the ESO's 3.6-meter telescope looms in the background. Why is it incredible? "Despite knowing about its 15-meter diameter beforehand, I was amazed by its size," Rodrigues noted in the ESO image release. The SEST first opened its great eye to the universe in 1987, at which time it was the only large telescope in the Southern Hemisphere tasked with collecting submillimeter wavelengths of light that exist beyond the visible light spectrum. These specific wavelengths of light are emitted by wandering comets and colossal clouds of cold molecular dust and gas threaded throughout the Milky Way and beyond. SEST's observations improved our knowledge of ancient galaxies, star formation and so much more, with its perch 2,375 meters (7,792 feet) above sea level granting it a near unrivalled view of the heavens above. The SEST telescope was decommissioned in 2003, though its work was continued by the more capable Atacama Pathfinder Experiment (APEX) and the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA). With its working days over, the SEST telescope now stands as a quiet mirror reflecting the stars of the Southern Hemisphere night sky, seemingly pondering mysteries of the universe that it once tried to solve
summary: Astronomer José Rodrigues captured a photograph of the decommissioned Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope at Chile's La Silla Observatory, showing stars and airglow reflected in its 15-meter dish. The image highlights the telescope's historical role in submillimeter astronomy before it was replaced by APEX and ALMA.
author: Space.com

title: South Park Episode 29 Addresses Beef Shortage With Diarrhea Gag
content: The 29th season has begun to slightly spin its wheels, but this poo-splattered episode suggests an imminent story arc: the release of Grand Theft Auto VI Are record beef shortages simply not that rich a topic for South Park to riff off? The show’s 29th season had its first outright middling episode this week with a zigzaggy outing that gestured vaguely toward the performative eating of particular foods, nodded slightly at a father-son story development, and wound it all up by repeating and amplifying a funny season-long running gag that increasingly seems like it will actually serve as a makeshift story arc. But let’s jump back to the beginning, perhaps the most laugh-out-loud moment of the episode: Cartman in a fugue of delight over the impending meal of sloppy joes at the school cafeteria, to which he forms a tribute in the form of a sloppy-joe-themed version of Gary Glitter’s Rock and Roll Part Two – a music clearance reaffirming that Trey Parker and Matt Stone don’t care if a song choice might make people tut-tut (because the singer is a serial sex offender) or just annoyed (because that song sucks). Cartman’s infectious glee is short-lived, however, when he’s informed that the lunch special for the day isn’t a sloppy joe after all, or anything beef-related, but cuy – Guinea Pig on a stick.
summary: The 29th season of South Park features an episode that addresses America's beef shortage and concludes with a recurring diarrhea gag. The review describes the episode as middling, noting it vaguely references performative eating and a father-son story development.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Olivia Colman stars in folk-horror romance The Wicker review
content:
Olivia Colman stars as a depressed and bullied fisherwoman in medieval England in the folk-horror romance Wicker. The film is adapted from the 2006 story The Wicker Husband by British writer Ursula Wills and features a mysterious basketmaker played by Peter Dinklage. According to the review, the narrative occupies a strange overlap between macabre horror and sentimentality, invoking the spirit of mystery author Shirley Jackson.

The story is set in a fabular medieval village characterized by bizarre patriarchal rituals, such as the placement of metal collars on new brides. Colman’s character lives alone in a remote cottage and brings her catch of tench and gudgeon to market, where she faces mockery and bullying from the local community. Among her tormentors are Richard E Grant, who plays a lazy and incompetent doctor, and Elizabeth Debicki, who portrays a spiteful tailor’s wife described as an elegant, sharp-faced woman.
summary: Olivia Colman plays a bullied medieval fisherwoman who finds a wicker lover in this folk-horror romance. The film is adapted from Ursula Wills' 2006 story and features Peter Dinklage and Alexander Skarsgård.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Underscores joins Charli xcx tour after acclaimed album U
content: With a sound inspired by the San Francisco tech boom, the hyperpop musician is entering the big leagues, and has a slot on Charli xcx’s tour. First she needs to get over her own shyness – not to mention a fear of love songs The life of a rising pop star: One day, you’re performing your own song with Charli xcx, her dancers emulating your choreography, an arena’s worth of fans screaming along. The next, you’re on a surgery table, with a healthcare professional yanking four superfluous teeth out of your mouth. Even pop stars need emergency dental work sometimes. It’s all par for the course for April Grey, the San Francisco-born, Chicago-based musician who records as Underscores. Her 2026 has been, plainly, wild: her third album, U, released in March, was met with acclaim and attracted a small army of new fans. Many of the shows on her tour in support of U, earlier this year, were upgraded due to demand, and one expects the bump she’ll get from her current run supporting Charli xcx’s Music, Fashion, Film tour will push her into even bigger rooms. It’s a blow-up befitting the level of ambition Grey put into U, which is a taut, compulsively listenable pop record that sounds like a mid-2000s Now That’s What I Call Music! Compilation as recreated by Aphex Twin. “As I was making it, it felt like a very big swing for the fences,” she says. “I wanted it to be big.”
summary: San Francisco-born musician Underscores has secured a slot on Charli xcx’s Music, Fashion, Film tour following the release of her third album, U. The hyperpop artist describes the record as a big swing for the fences that has attracted a new fan base and upgraded show sizes due to demand.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Best NFL Receivers in Their Prime Ranked, Excluding Veterans
content: The article ranks current top NFL wide receivers, noting that quarterbacks in 2026 have access to numerous high-caliber options. The analysis is limited to players in their prime years, explicitly excluding older but excellent receivers such as Mike Evans and Davante Adams.
summary: Quarterbacks in 2026 have a series of dazzling weapons at their disposal. The article ranks the best NFL receivers currently, limiting the list to players in their prime and leaving out older receivers such as Mike Evans and Davante Adams.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Brewers win World Series, exposing big-market bias
content:
Howard Bryant argues that the Milwaukee Brewers’ first World Series championship exposes the fallacy that small-market teams cannot compete against baseball’s oligarch class. The article contends that the sport’s leadership has long maintained that such an outcome was impossible, a stance that Bryant describes as undermining the Brewers, who led the standings for 149 days during the 2026 season. This narrative of a predetermined game persisted despite Milwaukee’s dominant performance, which included a franchise-record 103 regular-season wins and the fourth-most total wins in baseball since 2018.

Bryant highlights specific victories that demonstrate the Brewers' dominance, such as a 22-0 win over Seattle on August 18 and a 20-0 victory against Cincinnati a month later. The team secured their fourth consecutive National League Central title and their fifth in six years, finishing 14 games ahead of their division rivals. Despite these achievements, the article notes that baseball’s owners dismissed the Brewers' success as an illusion or an outlier. Even after Milwaukee swept the Dodgers in four games, ESPN’s Jeff Passan reported that the owners’ position remained unchanged, viewing the season as merely an appetizer for the offseason push toward implementing a salary cap.
summary: The Milwaukee Brewers won their first World Series by sweeping the Los Angeles Dodgers, a result that challenges the belief that small-market teams cannot compete. The article argues that baseball owners ignored the Brewers' dominant 103-win regular season and divisional success to maintain their stance on the game's competitive balance.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mussolini scores first Serie A goal in Lazio's 6-2 win over Sassuolo
content:
Lazio secured a decisive 6-2 victory over Sassuolo on Tuesday, a match highlighted by Mussolini’s first Serie A goal. Although home attendance has declined due to a dispute with the club’s owner, approximately 10,000 supporters traveled 300 kilometers to witness the high-scoring encounter.

The following day, Serie A recorded its second scoreless draw of the season as Parma and Udinese played to a stalemate at the Tardini. The match featured significant defensive efforts, including a penalty save by Maduka Okoye for Udinese, who were in the midst of a six-game losing streak, and a critical goalline clearance by Mariano Troilo for Parma.

In other action, Milan initially took the lead against Bologna at San Siro after coming from behind. However, the Rossoneri subsequently collapsed to suffer a 4-2 defeat in the match.
summary: Mussolini scored his first Serie A goal as Lazio defeated Sassuolo 6-2 on Tuesday. The match was highlighted by 10,000 Lazio fans traveling 300km to attend the game.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England coach urges nerve as 68‑point swing needed for Rugby League World Cup semi‑finals
content:
England head coach Brian McDermott has urged his team to maintain their composure as they seek a crucial victory against Tonga on Friday. A win is necessary to secure a remarkable qualification for the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals, a goal that now requires a 68-point swing in the final group games. McDermott described the current circumstances as a difficult situation to negotiate.

England’s path to the semi-finals was nearly closed following their opening defeat by Tonga two weeks ago. This early loss, combined with a complex and shortened 10-team tournament format, had appeared to consign the team to an early exit. However, an 82-0 victory over France last Saturday kept their hopes alive, though qualification remains unlikely.
summary: England must overcome a 68‑point deficit in their final group matches to stay in contention for the Rugby League World Cup semi‑finals. Coach Brian McDermott said the team must keep their nerve after a loss to Tonga and an 82‑0 win over France left qualification possible but unlikely.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ivan Toney to stand trial during Euro 2028 after denying assault charge
content:
England striker Ivan Toney has effectively been ruled out of Euro 2028, as his trial for assault occasioning actual bodily harm is scheduled to begin on 12 June 2028. Toney appeared at Southwark Crown Court, where he stood in the dock to confirm a not guilty plea.

The striker is accused of head-butting and punching Saber Da Silva at a Soho nightclub on 6 December last year.
summary: England striker Ivan Toney will stand trial for assault on 12 June 2028 and has denied the charges. He was accused of head‑butting and punching Saber Da Silva at a Soho nightclub on 6 December last year and has been ruled out of Euro 2028.
author: Guardian Sport

title: NWSL revises Rodman rule after Players Association grievance
content:
The National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) has revised its High Impact Player rule, eliminating the previous eight criteria that limited which players clubs could sign. This change, announced on Friday, resolves a grievance with the league’s Players Association, which argued that the initial criteria violated federal labor law. Consequently, starting next season, every player in the NWSL will qualify for the rule, allowing clubs to spend their resources on any player they choose.

The revision impacts teams like the Washington Spirit, who previously held a significant advantage in attendance due to their accessible stadium, large fanbase, and a roster featuring many players who met the original High Impact Player criteria, including Trinity Rodman. While the Spirit currently occupy a top-four position and are expected to draw full crowds at "Rowdy Audi" for upcoming matches against Chicago, the new rule ensures that no single club retains an exclusive roster advantage under the previous framework.
summary: The NWSL eliminated the eight specific criteria for High Impact Player status, allowing clubs to spend their money on any player they choose. This change was announced Friday to settle a grievance with the Players Association, which argued the initial criteria violated federal labor law.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Carrick keeps Fernandes as United captain, says no assurances needed on future
content:
Michael Carrick has confirmed he will not remove the Manchester United captaincy from Bruno Fernandes, despite dropping him for the recent defeat by Bournemouth. Carrick stated he is not surprised to remain in his role as head coach and described Fernandes as “important” to the squad. Following talks held this week, in which the Portuguese midfielder criticized tactics during a loss to Como, Fernandes was an unused substitute on Sunday.

Harry Maguire wore the armband during the Bournemouth match but will not retain it for Saturday’s game at Chelsea. Carrick indicated that “there is no decision to be made” regarding the leadership role and praised Fernandes, signaling that the captaincy remains secure.
summary: Michael Carrick confirmed Bruno Fernandes will retain the Manchester United captaincy after being dropped for the Bournemouth defeat. Carrick stated he is not surprised to remain head coach and said Fernandes is important to the squad.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Dundee United hold Celtic to draw, prompting midfield debate
content: Dundee United drew with reigning champions Celtic in Glasgow, prompting questions about whether the visitors possess Scotland's best midfield three.
summary: Dundee United drew with reigning champions Celtic in Glasgow. The result has raised the question of whether Dundee United possess Scotland's best midfield three.

title: England boss McDermott urges patience in PNG points chase
content: England head coach Brian McDermott has advised his players to remain calm while pursuing points against Papua New Guinea. The match is scheduled for Friday in Wollongong, with the result crucial for maintaining England's Rugby League World Cup aspirations.
summary: England boss Brian McDermott has urged his players not to panic while chasing points against Papua New Guinea. The match is scheduled for Friday in Wollongong to keep alive England's Rugby League World Cup hopes.

title: Rybakina Clinches Year-End Number One Ranking After Tokyo Win
content: Elena Rybakina has secured the year-end women's singles number one ranking. She achieved this milestone by defeating Yulia Putintseva in the last 16 round of the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo. The accomplishment was described as an amazing achievement.
summary: Elena Rybakina secured the year-end women's singles number one spot by defeating Yulia Putintseva. The victory occurred in the last 16 round of the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo.

title: Jake Paul to return to ring on 24 December
content: Jake Paul is scheduled to return to the ring on 24 December for the first time since his loss to Anthony Joshua. His upcoming opponent has not yet been confirmed.
summary: Jake Paul is scheduled to return to the ring on 24 December. This will be his first fight since losing to Anthony Joshua, and his opponent has yet to be confirmed.

title: Burnley faces potential third consecutive relegation to third tier
content: Back-to-back relegations to the third tier of English football are reportedly becoming more common. This season, Burnley could achieve a third consecutive drop, following Luton Town and Leicester.
summary: Back-to-back relegations to the third tier of English football are becoming more common. Burnley could make it a hat-trick after Luton Town and Leicester.

title: Gallup: Most voters report higher enthusiasm for midterm ballots than usual
content: A new Gallup survey indicates that most American voters report higher enthusiasm for casting ballots in this year’s midterms compared to previous elections. Specifically, 56 percent of respondents stated they were “more enthusiastic about voting than usual,” while 30 percent expressed being “less enthusiastic” and 11 percent indicated they were “as” enthusiastic.
summary: A new Gallup survey indicates that 56 percent of respondents are more enthusiastic about voting this year than usual. Conversely, 30 percent of respondents reported being less enthusiastic and 11 percent said they were as enthusiastic as usual.

title: NC 1st District Becomes Most Expensive US House Race
content: North Carolina’s 1st Congressional District has become the most expensive House race on record, according to new ad spending data. Democratic Rep. Don Davis is seeking reelection in the newly redrawn district against GOP challenger Laurie Buckhout, a retired Army colonel. A total of $52.9 million has been spent on the race.
summary: North Carolina’s 1st Congressional District has become the most expensive House race on record, according to new ad spending data shared this week. Democratic Rep.

content: The Hill’s senior vice president of editorial content, Bill Sammon, and co-hosts discuss reports that former Rep. Mary Peltola (D) recruited “spoiler” candidates to interfere in the Alaska Senate race against incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan (R). The live segment also features a final forecast for Tuesday’s midterms.

title: Trump rallies in South Carolina to support Sen. Darline Graham
content: President Trump is in South Carolina Thursday afternoon to bolster Republican support ahead of next week’s midterms. He is expected to campaign for Senator Darline Graham, the sister of the late Senator Lindsey Graham, who is facing a competitive challenge from Democrat Annie Andrews.
summary: President Trump is in South Carolina to campaign for Republican Sen. Darline Graham ahead of next week's midterms. He is expected to rally for Graham, who faces a competitive challenge from Democrat Annie Andrews.

title: Utah charges Kalshi, executives over illegal online gambling
content: Utah has filed criminal charges against prediction market platform Kalshi, CEO Tarek Mansour, and Chief Operating Officer Luana Lopes Lara. The state alleges the individuals illegally profited from promoting and offering online gambling within the jurisdiction. The defendants face 13 felony counts and one misdemeanor count as part of this legal action.
summary: Utah has brought criminal charges against Kalshi and its CEO Tarek Mansour and COO Luana Lopes Lara for allegedly profiting from illegal online gambling in the state. The charges include 13 felony counts and one misdemeanor count.

title: National Links Trust to End Operations at East Potomac Golf Links on Nov. 15
content: The National Links Trust announced it will cease operations at East Potomac Golf Links, Washington’s most popular public golf course, on Nov. 15. In a Thursday statement, the NLT noted that a new long‑term lease with the Interior Department and the National Park Service to manage and operate the site is part of the transition, as President Trump is reportedly eyeing the property for redevelopment.
summary: The National Links Trust announced it will cease operating the East Potomac Golf Links, Washington’s most popular public golf course, on Nov. 15. The move comes as President Trump eyes the property for redevelopment and the NLT referenced a new long‑term lease with the Interior Department and National Park Service.

title: Missouri abortion ban and California billionaire tax proposals appear on state ballots
content: Missouri and California voters will decide on significant ballot measures, including potential bans on abortion, new taxes on billionaire wealth, and restrictions concerning transgender individuals. In Missouri, the proposed abortion ban would follow the removal of a previous ban two years prior. Meanwhile, California residents may vote to impose a 5% wealth tax on billionaires.
summary: Missouri voters could approve a ban on abortion, reversing a ban that was removed two years ago. California voters could approve a measure to tax billionaires at 5% of their wealth.
author: NPR Politics

title: Study: Nearly half of severely distressed AI users seek emotional support from chatbots
content: A new study reveals that nearly one-third of Israeli adults using generative AI tools seek emotional support, coping advice, or mental health assistance from platforms like ChatGPT and Gemini. Among those experiencing severe psychological distress, this figure rises to almost half. The research was conducted by Tel-Hai University of Kiryat Shmona in the Galilee along with collaborating institutions.
summary: A study found that almost one in three Israeli adults using generative AI tools seek emotional support or mental health assistance from platforms like ChatGPT. Among users experiencing severe psychological distress, the percentage seeking this support rose to nearly one in two.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Complex medication regimens linked to greater physician burden in home care
content: Patients receiving home-based medical care, often older adults with multiple chronic conditions, frequently experience polypharmacy, defined as the concurrent use of multiple medications. While this practice is prevalent in this population, the associated challenges of medication management extend beyond merely the number of prescribed drugs.
summary: Patients receiving home-based medical care are often older adults with multiple chronic conditions and prevalent polypharmacy. The challenges of medication management for these patients extend beyond the number of prescribed medications.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Flinders University warns autistic adults face elevated cybercrime risks
content: Flinders University experts warn that autistic adults face elevated risks of involvement in cyber-related crime. The research suggests these individuals may fall into such criminal activities unwittingly.
summary: Flinders University experts warn that autistic adults may have elevated risks of being involved in cyber-related crime. These individuals might fall into such crimes unwittingly.
author: Medical Xpress

title: GLP-1 drugs help bariatric surgery patients lose regained weight
content: A study involving researchers from the Regenstrief Institute, Indiana University, Purdue University, and the University of Florida suggests that GLP-1 medications may assist patients in losing weight regained after bariatric surgery. The research indicates that individuals prescribed these glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists lost more of their regained weight over six and 12 months compared to similar patients who did not use the drugs.
summary: A study by researchers at Regenstrief Institute, Indiana University, Purdue University, and the University of Florida found that GLP-1 medications benefit those who regain weight after bariatric surgery. Patients prescribed these drugs lost more regained weight over six and 12 months than comparable patients who did not use them.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Permanent DST bill passed by House could add two billion dark school commutes
content: The U.S. House of Representatives passed a bill last summer to make daylight saving time permanent in the United States, eliminating the practice of turning back the clocks each fall. Nineteen states, including Washington, have already preapproved this change. If the bill is ultimately signed into law, the permanent daylight saving time would go into effect in those states.
summary: Permanent DST bill passed by House could add two billion dark school commutes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Hidden brain rhythm in macaques challenges consciousness theories
content: New research by Janis Hesse at the University of California, Berkeley, and colleagues aims to address the mystery of how brains give rise to consciousness. The study, which involves macaque monkeys, suggests that a hidden brain rhythm challenges existing ideas about the origins of consciousness.
summary: New research by Janis Hesse at the University of California, Berkeley, and colleagues may help explain how brains give rise to consciousness. The study's insights are derived from research conducted on macaque monkeys.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Brain scans reveal silent strokes and benign tumors in healthy adults
content: In 2007, Dutch researchers scanned the brains of 2,000 individuals aged 45 and older who were living ordinary lives. The study revealed that seven percent of participants had signs of a stroke they were unaware of. Additionally, nearly two percent had a small bulge in a blood vessel, while a similar number possessed a benign tumor.
summary: A 2007 study in the Netherlands found that seven in every 100 adults aged 45 and over had signs of a stroke they were unaware of. The scan also identified small blood vessel bulges and benign tumors in nearly two in every 100 participants.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Iron-based MRI agent slows heart scarring in lab-grown human tissue
content:
A research group at Ikerbasque, led by Aitziber L. Cortajarena, has developed an iron-based magnetic resonance imaging contrast agent designed for both diagnostic and therapeutic applications. The team, specializing in Biomolecular Nanotechnology, tested this new agent on lab-grown human heart tissue to evaluate its efficacy in addressing cardiac fibrosis.

The study demonstrated that the agent accumulates specifically within fibrotic tissue. Additionally, the MRI signal intensity of the agent increased as the severity of the disease progressed. The research further confirmed that the contrast agent successfully slowed the progression of the condition in the tested tissue.
summary: The Biomolecular Nanotechnology research group, led by Ikerbasque research professor Aitziber L. Cortajarena, developed an iron‑based MRI contrast agent that accumulates in fibrotic heart tissue. In lab‑grown human heart tissue, the agent’s signal intensity rises with disease severity and it slows disease progression.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Concern over cut to Card Before You Leave mental health crisis scheme
content: Concern has been raised over a proposed cut to the Card Before You Leave scheme, which supports young people in mental health crises. The scheme guarantees that those presenting at a hospital emergency department receive a written appointment with specialists before they leave.
summary: There is concern about a cut to the Card Before You Leave scheme for young people's mental health crises. The scheme ensures that young people who present at a hospital emergency department in a mental health crisis receive a written appointment with specialists before leaving.
author: BBC Health

title: Europe’s central bank chief Christine Lagarde to step down nine months early
content: Christine Lagarde, the president of the European Central Bank, will step down from her role on 7 February 2027, nine months before her term was originally scheduled to end in October. The ECB announced the decision on Thursday, bringing an end to months of speculation regarding her future. Lagarde is currently viewed as a candidate to take over the World Economic Forum. This departure occurs while the eurozone continues to face challenges with weak growth and inflation.
summary: Europe’s central bank chief Christine Lagarde to step down nine months early.
author: Guardian Business

title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $17 billion
content: Acquisition will supercharge DoorDash’s grocery delivery, ‘one of the hardest things to get right online’, CEO says DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17bn acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said.
summary: DoorDash is acquiring Instacart in a $17 billion deal that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. The Instacart brand and app will remain, and customers will gain access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash.
author: Guardian Business

title: FTC Orders Delta, Uber, and Nine Other Companies to Disclose Algorithmic Pricing Data
content:
The Federal Trade Commission has issued a demand to nine major US companies, including Delta, United, JetBlue, Lyft, Uber, DoorDash, Instacart, Target, and Walmart, to disclose how they utilize algorithms and loyalty programs. The regulator is seeking explanations for why these entities charge different prices for identical products or services and vary wages for drivers based on personal histories.

This inquiry follows prior investigations and lawsuits alleging that consumers face price discrimination based on their buying histories and that drivers receive different fares due to their personal records. The FTC’s move targets some of the nation’s largest airlines, ride-share platforms, and retailers to uncover the mechanisms behind these algorithmic pricing practices.
summary: The Federal Trade Commission is demanding that nine major companies, including Delta, Uber, and Walmart, explain how they use algorithms and loyalty programs to set variable prices and wages. This inquiry follows investigations and lawsuits alleging that consumers and drivers face different costs based on their personal histories.
author: Guardian Business

title: US GDP grows 3.4% in Q3, September inflation rises to 3.7%
content:
The US economy expanded at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, surpassing the 3.2% pace forecast by economists polled by Reuters. This data, released by the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis on Thursday, coincided with reports that inflation accelerated to 3.7% in September. The release occurred less than a week before the midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress.

These economic figures contrast with a sharp deterioration in consumer sentiment as the elections approach. The Commerce Department data highlights a divergence between robust GDP growth and rising inflation, providing a mixed economic backdrop ahead of the upcoming vote.
summary: US GDP grows 3.4% in Q3, September inflation rises to 3.7%.
author: Guardian Business

title: Ralph Nader warns conditions are worse as he challenges Democrats ahead of 2026 midterms
content:
Ralph Nader, the former presidential candidate and consumer-rights advocate, argues that the issues driving his 2000 campaign are now more severe than ever ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections. He cites a corporate plutocracy, a broken healthcare system, massive inequality, and cash-soaked elections as key problems. Nader also notes that many people are angry about their inability to pay bills and are disgusted with lawmakers in Washington DC.

Nader states that these conditions are nearly identical to those that prompted his previous presidential run, which he describes as making him a political pariah in Washington. However, he asserts that the situation is now much, much worse. The former candidate emphasizes the need to “really change things for the working class” as he issues a challenge to Democrats in the upcoming election cycle.
summary: Ralph Nader states that issues like corporate power and broken healthcare are worse now than during his 2000 presidential run. He asserts these conditions will push him to challenge Democrats in the upcoming 2026 midterm elections.
author: Guardian Business

title: New harmonic increment method improves smooth approximations of minimum function
content:
A recent paper published in the Journal of Inequalities and Applications introduces a new method for improving smooth approximations of the minimum function. Prof. Thomas A. Weber demonstrates how a harmonic-increment transformation enhances these calculations for systems limited by their smallest input.

The technique brings any smooth estimate that lies strictly below the minimum closer to the actual value. Crucially, the improved estimate remains below the minimum, ensuring it stays a conservative estimate of a worst realization, or weakest link.
summary: A harmonic increment provides a new way to improve smooth approximations of the minimum function. In a recent paper, published in the Journal of Inequalities and Applications, Prof.

title: Emory physicists propose light method to detect anyons for quantum computing
content: Theoretical physicists at Emory University have developed a method to use light to detect the "spectral fingerprints" of anyons, which are exotic quasiparticles arising from the collective behavior of many electrons. Published in Physical Review Letters, this work provides a new tool for studying anyons, which have potential as fundamental building blocks for quantum computing.
summary: Theoretical physicists at Emory University have developed a method to use light to detect the spectral fingerprints of anyons. Their findings, published in Physical Review Letters, offer a new tool for studying these quasiparticles which hold potential as building blocks for quantum computing.
author: Phys.org

title: What makes forest protection work?
content: A new study by the Institute for Food and Resource Economics at the University of Bonn indicates that the success of nature conservation measures is partly determined by the credible enforcement of environmental laws.
summary: A new study from the Institute for Food and Resource Economics at the University of Bonn shows that the success of nature conservation measures depends partly on the credible enforcement of environmental laws.
author: Phys.org

title: Permanent DST bill puts U.S. schoolchildren at risk by forcing pre-sunrise commutes
content:
A new analysis published in Current Biology on October 29 warns that making daylight saving time permanent would endanger millions of U.S. schoolchildren. The study examines the implications of the Sunshine Protection Act, which the U.S. House passed in July 2026. According to the report, this legislation would force students to leave for school before sunrise for much of the academic year.

The analysis indicates that these earlier departure times coincide with periods when fatal crashes involving pedestrians are more likely. Consequently, the permanent shift to daylight saving time could significantly increase safety risks for children commuting to school in the dark.
summary: Permanent DST bill puts U.S. schoolchildren at risk by forcing pre-sunrise commutes.
author: Phys.org

title: Experts warn underpreparing for severe climate risks can cost the UK far more than overpreparing
content: Experts in climate, nature, health, national security and financial risk have co‑authored a commentary in Nature Climate Change urging a more integrated approach to UK government climate and nature risk assessments. They argue that conflicting advice can present policymakers with very different pictures of future risk severity, complicating decisions about the seriousness of action and the level of spending required. The authors warn that, for the United Kingdom, underpreparing for severe climate risks could cost far more than the expense of overpreparing.
summary: Experts warn underpreparing for severe climate risks can cost the UK far more than overpreparing.
author: Phys.org

title: Ultrathin carbon ribbons conduct electricity like metals in first successful synthesis
content: As modern electronic devices shrink, the metal electrical wires inside them face significant challenges. These conventional wires generate excessive heat and experience a massive spike in electrical resistance, which negatively affects overall performance as their size decreases.
summary: Scientists have achieved the first successful synthesis of ultrathin carbon ribbons that conduct electricity like metals. Conventional metal wires in shrinking electronic devices generate excessive heat and experience a spike in electrical resistance.
author: Phys.org

title: ISTA study links stars' evolutionary history to magnetic field estimates
content: A new study published in Astronomy & Astrophysics by researchers at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) highlights the impact of stellar evolutionary history on magnetic field estimates. Magnetic fields are present in many stars, including the sun, but remain poorly understood and are rarely included in stellar evolution models, which limits their accuracy. The research suggests that a star's "criminal" evolutionary history is crucial for correctly interpreting its internal magnetic fields.
summary: A new study by researchers at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria shows that a star's evolutionary history is crucial for interpreting its internal magnetic fields. The research, published in Astronomy & Astrophysics, addresses why magnetic fields are too poorly understood to be reliably included in stellar evolution models.
author: Phys.org

title: Key oddity of quantum physics may run even deeper than anticipated
content: Quantum mechanics is distinguished by its probabilistic nature, a characteristic that sets it apart from other physical theories. A new analysis indicates that this specific property may originate from the mathematical foundations of the theory, running deeper than previously anticipated.
summary: Key oddity of quantum physics may run even deeper than anticipated.
author: New Scientist

title: Weakened brain signal may link schizophrenia symptoms
content: Scientists have identified a weakened brain signal that may link several seemingly unrelated schizophrenia symptoms, including sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and greater symptom severity. This discovery could help explain the disorder's underlying mechanisms and potentially facilitate earlier detection and the development of new treatments.
summary: Scientists identified a weakened brain signal that may connect sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and symptom severity in schizophrenia. This discovery could help explain the disorder's mechanisms and lead to earlier detection and new treatments.
author: Science Daily

title: UIC study finds cranberry juice slows dental plaque bacteria regrowth
content:
Researchers at the University of Illinois Chicago have found that pure, unsweetened cranberry juice can help protect teeth from decay. The study revealed that the juice slows the regrowth of dental plaque bacteria and reduces their production of acids that damage tooth enamel. This discovery adds a new potential benefit to cranberry juice, which is already known for helping prevent urinary tract infections.

The protective effect may be attributed to naturally occurring compounds called proanthocyanidins. These substances interfere with harmful bacteria, thereby mitigating the acid production responsible for enamel erosion.
summary: Researchers at the University of Illinois Chicago found that pure, unsweetened cranberry juice reduces acid production and slows the regrowth of dental plaque bacteria. The effect is attributed to naturally occurring compounds called proanthocyanidins that interfere with harmful bacteria.
author: Science Daily

title: Less than 42 minutes of bright daylight linked to higher dementia risk
content: A study involving more than 87,000 adults indicates that higher daytime light exposure is associated with a 16% lower risk of dementia. The research found that longer exposure to bright light was linked to even greater reductions in this risk. Notably, getting less than 42 minutes of bright daylight daily emerged as a stronger predictor of dementia than six established risk factors.
summary: A study of more than 87,000 adults found that higher daytime light exposure was associated with a 16% lower risk of dementia. Getting less than 42 minutes of bright daylight daily was a stronger predictor of dementia than six established risk factors.
author: Science Daily

title: 700,000-year-old elephant tooth found in Israel reveals lush prehistoric world
content: A 700,000-year-old straight-tusked elephant tooth discovered in northern Israel reveals a lush prehistoric environment where giant elephants and early humans coexisted. Found alongside ancient stone tools, the remarkably preserved artifact belonged to one of the largest land mammals of the Ice Age.
summary: A remarkably preserved straight-tusked elephant tooth dating back nearly 700,000 years was discovered in northern Israel alongside ancient stone tools. The find reveals a surprisingly lush prehistoric environment where giant elephants and early humans lived together.
author: Science Daily

title: 128,000-year-old ice found in Tibet could rewrite climate history
content: Ancient ice discovered high in Tibet is estimated to be more than 128,000 years old, preserving a climate record scientists previously believed was lost. This finding offers a rare glimpse into the last ice age and may reshape understanding of how glaciers survive dramatic global climate changes.

title: NASA Juno Finds Jupiter's Complex Plasma Shield Differs from Earth's
content: NASA’s Juno spacecraft has identified a complex system of powerful plasma waves and multiple shock regions that Jupiter uses to defend against the solar wind. These findings highlight significant differences between Jupiter and Earth, potentially aiding scientists in understanding the massive shock waves generated by exploding stars.
summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft discovered that Jupiter uses a complex system of plasma waves and multiple shock regions to defend against the solar wind. These findings reveal major differences between Jupiter and Earth and may help scientists understand shock waves from exploding stars.

title: Mathematicians Find Flaw in Standard Model That Could Eliminate Need for Dark Energy
content:
Mathematicians have identified a potential fundamental flaw in the standard model of the universe, which could challenge the necessity of dark energy. Their calculations indicate that the mathematical framework describing cosmic expansion is inherently unstable. Consequently, the universe might accelerate naturally under Einstein’s original theory of gravity, rather than requiring an additional force to explain its expansion.

These findings also introduce questions regarding the assumption that our location in the universe is ordinary. By suggesting that cosmic acceleration can be explained without dark energy, the research proposes an alternative interpretation of the universe's dynamics based on existing gravitational theories.
summary: Mathematicians argue that the standard model of the universe contains a fundamental flaw that challenges the need for dark energy. Their calculations suggest that the universe could accelerate naturally under Einstein's original theory of gravity, raising questions about the ordinariness of our location in the universe.
author: Science Daily

title: Study Links Six Popular Sugar Substitutes to Faster Brain Aging
content: A study of nearly 13,000 adults found that individuals consuming the most artificial sweeteners experienced a 62% faster decline in memory and thinking skills. This decline was equivalent to approximately 1.6 additional years of brain aging. The research linked six popular sugar substitutes to this accelerated cognitive decline, raising concerns about long-term brain health effects, though causation was not established.
summary: Study Links Six Popular Sugar Substitutes to Faster Brain Aging.

title: Dame Sue Black Discusses Court Challenges in Forensic Anthropology Podcast
content:

In a podcast interview with Ian Sample, the professor discusses the challenges of testifying in court.

Black describes standing before a judge and jury as one of the most terrifying aspects of her career. She also addresses the reputational risks associated with presenting evidence in legal proceedings. Additionally, she offers insights into the potential future of forensic science. The podcast is available for order from the Guardian bookshop.
