title: NASA Welcomes Jared Spiers as Civil Servant After Contractor Transition
content:
Jared Spiers has transitioned from a contractor to a NASA civil servant at the agency’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. This change occurred in June 2026 as part of an administrator’s directive aimed at strengthening technical core competencies within the civil service workforce. Spiers currently serves as an electrical engineering technician, a role he has held since graduating from Pearl River Community College in 2017, where he earned three associate degrees in instrumentation, electronics, and electrical technology. He began his career at NASA Stennis the Monday following his graduation.

Spiers has contributed to NASA’s lunar return mission through his work at the Thad Cochran Test Stand, a facility originally built to test Saturn V rocket stages during the Apollo Program. He helped prepare the stand for the Green Run test series of the first core stage for the Space Launch System rocket prior to the successful Artemis I test flight. His work also laid the foundation for the Artemis II test flight around the Moon in April 2026, during which the first astronauts to fly aboard the Orion spacecraft traveled farther in space than humans had before.

Currently, Spiers works 12-hour shifts starting at 6 a.m. as part of the team preparing the test stand for stage testing of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket. This commercial partnership supports NASA’s goal of landing American astronauts on the Moon and building a Moon Base. His daily responsibilities include ensuring facility electronics are operational to collect accurate data, running conduit and cabling, connecting data-collecting instruments, and verifying that motor valves operate as intended.

The move to civil servant status has increased Spiers’ sense of ownership and pride in his work. Although he noted that he was never treated differently while a contractor, he feels more integrated into the team as a civil servant. This family-oriented mindset extends to his personal life, where his father, Joey Spiers, also transitioned from a longtime contractor to a civil servant in the summer of 2026 and works as an electrical engineering technician. Additionally, Spiers’ brother-in-law, Brock Sheppard, joined NASA as a mechanical engineering technician in September 2026.

Spiers actively mentors others and shares his professional journey with the community. During NASA’s Career Technical Education Day at Stennis in September 2026, he spoke to community college students and a virtual audience of thousands about his path to NASA, the importance of a strong work ethic, and how technical skills contribute to the agency’s mission. He credits veteran employees who mentored him early in his career for his current success and views his current crew as extended family.
summary: Jared Spiers, an electrical engineering technician at NASA’s Stennis Space Center, transitioned from a contractor to a civil servant in June 2026. He is currently part of the team preparing the Thad Cochran Test Stand for stage testing of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket.
author: NASA News

title: Hubble Image of Gravitational Lens Preps NASA's Roman Space Telescope
content:
NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope captured a sweeping barred galaxy in the center of an image taken on Oct. 22, 2026, with a vivid gravitational lens appearing in the bottom‑right corner. The picture was produced by NASA, ESA, and X. Huang of the University of San Francisco, and processed by Gladys Kober of NASA/Catholic University of America.

This observation is one of many gravitational‑lensing images collected by Hubble in preparation for science with the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Astronomers plan to use these images to analyze gravitational distortions, learn more about dark matter in the foreground galaxies, and lay the groundwork for future Roman observations.

The images illustrate how Hubble and Roman will work together to build a more comprehensive picture of the cosmos, as noted by the image credit to NASA, ESA, and X. Huang, with processing by Gladys Kober.
summary: Hubble captured a sinuous spiral galaxy and a vivid gravitational lens in the same field of view on Oct. 22, 2026. The image is part of a series of gravitational lensing observations that will help astronomers study dark matter and prepare for future Roman Space Telescope observations.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Releases 2026 ISAM State of Play, 368‑Page Industry Standard for Space Servicing
content:
NASA’s Langley Research Center has released the 2026 edition of the In-Space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing (ISAM) State of Play, a comprehensive document that has evolved into a primary industry resource. Dale Arney, senior team lead for the ISAM Technology Portfolio at NASA Langley, noted that the team recognized an inflection point when companies began requesting access to the report for competitive intelligence. Although some unnamed companies inquired about proprietary information, Arney confirmed that the document contains no such data. This impartiality is cited as a key factor in the report’s value to an industry seeking to understand a rapidly expanding field.

Published annually since 2021, the 2026 edition has expanded to 368 pages and documents current capabilities across 11 functional areas, including robotic manipulation, refueling, and structural assembly. The cover of the document features Astronaut F. Story Musgrave, who anchored on the Space Shuttle Endeavor’s robotic arm during the 1993 servicing mission of the Hubble Space Telescope. Arney described the field as having expanded more than linearly since the report’s inception. What started as a tool to ensure NASA centers shared a common reference point has become the industry’s go-to resource for distinguishing between what is currently possible and what remains conceptual.

The ISAM State of Play team enforces strict entry criteria for inclusion, requiring that hardware physically exist as either ground prototypes or in-flight demonstrations. Arney stated that the team rejects submissions consisting solely of PowerPoint presentations of technology ideas without evidence of actual work. Concepts that do not meet these hardware requirements are deferred until the following year’s review. This rigor is considered essential because ISAM capabilities are intended to enable missions that are impossible with traditional single-launch approaches, such as telescopes larger than any launch vehicle fairing, mobile national security assets, and commercial systems capable of on-orbit upgrades without full replacement.

John Mulvaney, a team member, described the document as a "crowdsource document" that relies on annual interviews with industry partners to ensure accuracy and completeness. Contributions to the report come from various NASA centers, including Ames, Glenn, Marshall, Kennedy, and Johnson, as well as international developers who meet the hardware criteria. The 2026 edition includes developer profiles and facilities documentation, providing mission designers with information on who is performing the work and where the facilities are located. This collaborative approach aims to offer both competitive context and collaboration opportunities for companies entering or expanding within the ISAM ecosystem.

The report serves as a technical reference and a roadmap for technologies that enable spacecraft to be serviced, assembled, and manufactured in orbit rather than launched as integrated systems. As the space industry moves toward more ambitious missions, including lunar infrastructure and on-orbit manufacturing, the ISAM State of Play provides a shared vocabulary and capability baseline. Arney emphasized that the document is not speculation about the future but rather documentation of what exists now and where the hardware is heading next. The 2026 ISAM State of Play is available for download at NASA.gov.
summary: NASA Releases 2026 ISAM State of Play, 368‑Page Industry Standard for Space Servicing.
author: NASA News

title: NASA invites public to send names on microchip aboard Dragonfly mission to Titan
content: The “Journey to Titan” campaign offers the public the opportunity to fly their names on a microchip with NASA’s Dragonfly mission. The chip will ride aboard the Dragonfly rotorcraft as it explores Saturn’s moon Titan by air. Credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins APL You may never soar under the clouds or over the organic sands of Saturn’s moon Titan, but your name can. NASA is inviting the public to send their names aboard the agency’s Dragonfly rotorcraft and be part of the first science mission to fly and explore the surface of another world. To have your name included on a microchip aboard Dragonfly and receive a personalized digital boarding pass commemorating your place on this historic mission, visit: https://go. Nasa. Gov/dragonfly-names “NASA’s Dragonfly mission will simply blow your mind,” said Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “By flying the first-ever rotorcraft science mission, NASA will explore Saturn’s largest moon, Titan, as we search for signs of habitability on a distant world that is most similar to our own. We are excited to bring humanity along for the journey of a lifetime, and we invite everyone to send their names on this small, but mighty rotorcraft that will unlock the secrets of the universe in what is widely considered one of the most exciting space missions of our lifetime.” The public can secure a place on Dragonfly’s passenger list until 11:59 p. M. EST Jan. 15, 2027. The Dragonfly rotorcraft is currently being assembled at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland. Scheduled to launch in 2028, the rotorcraft will travel to Titan, a remarkable world with a thick atmosphere, rivers and lakes of liquid methane, sweeping dunes, and a landscape rich in organic material. After arriving in 2034, Dragonfly will fly to different locations on the moon, exploring Titan’s diverse environments and searching for clues about prebiotic chemistry — the chemistry that came before biology — to help scientists better understand the ingredients and conditions for life. Dragonfly is being designed and built under the direction of APL, which leads the mission for NASA. Elizabeth Turtle of APL is the principal investigator. Dragonfly is the fourth mission in NASA’s New Frontiers Program, managed by NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, for the agency’s Science Mission Directorate. For more information on NASA’s Dragonfly mission, visit: https://science. Nasa. Gov/mission/dragonfly/ -end- Karen Fox / Molly Wasser Headquarters, Washington 240-285-5155 / 240-419-1732 karen. C. Fox@nasa. Gov / molly. L. Wasser@nasa. Gov Mike Buckley Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory 443-567-3145 michael. Buckley@jhuapl. Edu Share Details Last Updated Oct 29, 2026 Editor Jessica Taveau Location NASA Headquarters Related Terms Dragonfly Marshall Space Flight Center Saturn Saturn Moons Science Mission Directorate Titan
summary: The “Journey to Titan” campaign offers the public the opportunity to fly their names on a microchip with NASA’s Dragonfly mission. The chip will ride aboard the Dragonfly rotorcraft as it explores Saturn’s moon Titan by air.

title: 41,000 DHS employees and contractors exposed in massive data leak
content:
A large data breach has revealed the identities of more than 41,000 employees or contractors who work for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and its component agencies. The leaked files contain email addresses, phone numbers, office addresses, and references to internal systems, as well as sensitive information about undercover and surveillance programs. The data provides a detailed map of DHS’s organizational structure and operational procedures.

The records cover DHS itself and seven of its component agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). They were last updated on August 19, 2026.

The archive, titled “Icepick,” was published by the transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets) on Wednesday. Cybersecurity researcher and journalist maia arson crimew previewed the data for WIRED, saying it was obtained from a group that calls itself the Department of Peace. DDoSecrets stated that the data came from DHS’s Okta login system, and the hackers included a note that read, “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs.”
summary: An unprecedented leak of Department of Homeland Security records exposed details of more than 41,000 employees or contractors, including email addresses, phone numbers, and office addresses. The leak, released by DDoSecrets as “Icepick,” was sourced from DHS's Okta login system and includes references to internal systems and undercover surveillance programs.

title: Night Plane review: indie horror game puts players on a doomed jumbo jet
content: Liquid Static Studio; PC You take on the role of flight attendant in this clever and absorbing retro-style game that veers from daft horror spoof to genuinely disturbing There was always something creepy about the job-simulator genre. All those mindless automatons queueing up to use your bus, bar or bed store, or whatever workplace you are trapped in for the duration of the game. The endless repetitive tasks. The emptiness of the world beyond your corporate existence. Together, these elements scream existential terror … which is perhaps why we are now seeing a new indie sub-genre of job sim horror games, including Home Safety Hotline, Dredge and more recently, Grease Trap ’99, a Lovecraftian mystery set in a Scottish chip shop. Now, we have Night Plane, in which you take on the role of a flight attendant on a jumbo jet to hell. It all starts kind of normally. You turn up for the first day of your new job, meet your colleagues, then take your spot at the departure gate, checking in customers and being careful to root out anyone with invalid tickets. Once on the plane, you roll your trolley down the aisle, serving booze and inedible meals, and occasionally dealing with passenger complaints. Then the plane crashes and, frankly, it all goes downhill from there.
summary: Night Plane is a retro‑style PC game by Liquid Static Studio that lets you play as a flight attendant on a jumbo jet. The game begins with routine duties such as checking tickets and serving passengers before the plane crashes and the experience becomes disturbing.

title: Spain train collision near Toledo kills 68; cranes clear wreckage through night
content: Rescue teams worked through the night at the site of a train collision near Toledo that killed 68 people. Cranes continued clearing the twisted wreckage while authorities set up a temporary morgue to identify the victims.
summary: Rescue teams worked through the night at the site of a train collision near Toledo that killed 68 people. Cranes continued clearing the wreckage as authorities set up a temporary morgue to identify victims.
author: Euronews

title: Tel Aviv protesters call for Arab-Jewish unity government after inconclusive election
content: Protesters gathered on the streets of Tel Aviv demanding a government that unites Jewish and Arab parties following an Israeli election that produced no clear winner. Police intervened to disperse activists who were blocking traffic.
summary: Protesters took to the streets of Tel Aviv to demand a government bringing together Jewish and Arab parties. Police moved in to disperse activists blocking traffic after Israel's election produced no clear winner.
author: Euronews

title: Fuel crisis strands 200 passengers on MV Odyssey in Cambodia
content: Around 200 passengers on the residential cruise ship MV Odyssey have been left stranded in Cambodia after the vessel’s operator halted operations, citing soaring fuel costs. The Odyssey, which began a continuous world voyage from Belfast in October 2024, carries residents who have paid six‑figure sums for their cabins.
summary: Around 200 passengers on the residential cruise ship MV Odyssey were left stranded in Cambodia after its operator suspended operations amid soaring fuel costs. The ship began its continuous world voyage from Belfast in October 2024, with some residents paying six‑figure sums for cabins.
author: Euronews

title: JD Vance writes to Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei to revive peace talks
content: The Wall Street Journal reports that JD Vance has written to senior Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei in an effort to revive negotiations, a move noted as occurring less than a week before the U.S. congressional midterm elections. The report adds that former President Donald Trump continues to warn of possible renewed strikes.
summary: JD Vance has written to senior Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei in a bid to revive negotiations. The Wall Street Journal reports the move comes less than a week before the US congressional midterm elections as Trump continues to warn of possible renewed strikes again.
author: Euronews

title: Visitors to Amsterdam's Rembrandt House Museum can get his art as tattoos
content: Visitors to Amsterdam’s Rembrandt House Museum can now take home a piece of the Dutch master’s art in the form of a permanent tattoo. The museum offers the option for guests to have Rembrandt’s masterpieces inked onto their skin.
summary: Visitors to the Rembrandt House Museum in Amsterdam can once again take home a piece of the Dutch master's art as a permanent tattoo. The tattoos let them carry Rembrandt's masterpieces on their skin.
author: Euronews

title: Serbia’s Student List confronts foreign policy, governing challenges after win
content: Serbia’s Student List has won an election, a result the source says has fundamentally changed the country’s political landscape. The victory, however, is described as possibly the easier part, as the student movement now faces foreign‑policy and governing challenges.
summary: The victory of Serbia’s Student List has fundamentally changed the country’s political landscape. Winning the election may prove to have been the easier part.
author: Euronews

title: Albanian opposition MPs disrupt parliament with smoke flares, protest police violence
content: Opposition MPs disrupted a parliamentary session in Albania, brandishing smoke flares and showing photographs of injured protesters. They accused the police of using violence against demonstrators who were calling for Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation.
summary: Opposition MPs disrupted a parliamentary session in Albania by brandishing smoke flares and displaying photographs of injured protesters. They accused police of using violence against demonstrators demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation.
author: Euronews

title: DRC opposition coalition C64 meets in Rome, urges inclusive dialogue
content: The Democratic Republic of Congo’s main opposition coalition, C64, convened in Rome on Tuesday. Its five leaders, speaking from the Italian capital amid pressure to respond to Joseph Kabila’s rebellion, condemned any seizure of power by force and urged an inclusive dialogue, according to FRANCE 24’s Emmet Livingston.
summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's main opposition coalition, C64, met in Rome on Tuesday. Its five leaders condemned any seizure of power by force and called for inclusive dialogue in response to Joseph Kabila’s rebellion.
author: France 24

title: Putin hosts Russia-Africa summit to expand ties with African nations
content: Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted dozens of African leaders on Wednesday at a Russia‑Africa summit, describing the meeting as part of Moscow’s effort to expand its influence across the continent. The summit is presented as a renewed Kremlin initiative to bolster ties with Africa’s nearly 1.6 billion people, which the Kremlin views as increasingly assertive on the global stage.
summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted dozens of African leaders at a Russia-Africa summit on Wednesday. The summit is part of Moscow’s renewed effort to bolster ties with the African continent.
author: France 24

title: Getty Museum to display masterpieces on six Paris façades
content: In this edition of Entre Nous, curator David‑Hervé Boutin of “L’art dans la ville” discusses the Getty Museum’s initiative to bring its collection to Paris streets. Masterpieces will be installed on six city façades, creating an open‑air art experience across the French capital.
summary: Curator David-Hervé Boutin of "L'art dans la ville" explains how the Getty Museum is bringing its collection to the streets of Paris. Masterpieces will be shown on six of the city’s façades, creating an open‑air art experience throughout the French capital.
author: France 24

title: Donald Trump avoids Epstein case as DOJ releases 3 million court documents during midterms
content:
The mid‑term election campaign is in full swing in the United States, yet Donald Trump is reportedly doing his utmost to avoid one subject: the Epstein Files.  

On January 30, the U.S. Department of Justice published the court records related to the Epstein case. At France 24, journalists Samia Metheni and Ava Luquet examined the 3 million documents to understand how Epstein’s network operated.  

They discussed what they found while reviewing the documents and addressed the impact those findings still have on Trump, with Ava Luquet answering questions from François Picard.
summary: The midterm elections campaign is in full swing in the United States, but Donald Trump is doing his utmost to avoid one subject: the Epstein Files. On January 30, the US Department of Justice published the court records relating to the Epstein case.
author: France 24

title: Journalist calls for real questions after Spain train collision kills at least 68
content: In this edition of Perspective, we focus on the tragic train collision that killed at least 68 people in Spain on Wednesday. We're joined by Nicholas Kingsley, executive editor of Railway Gazette International.
summary: The train collision in Spain on Wednesday killed at least 68 people. Nicholas Kingsley, executive editor of Railway Gazette International, discussed the incident on Perspective.
author: France 24

title: France may advance 2027 minimum wage rise to December amid protest plans
content: The French government is seeking ways to ease social unrest ahead of cost‑of‑living demonstrations scheduled for this weekend. While the minimum wage was slated to rise on 1 January 2027, officials are now weighing an earlier implementation—about a month sooner—and an additional increase.
summary: The French government is seeking ways to calm social unrest ahead of cost‑of‑living demonstrations scheduled for the weekend. Officials are considering moving the minimum‑wage increase, originally set for Jan 1 2027, forward by one month and adding an extra boost.
author: France 24

title: Trump and Obama trade barbs as US midterm elections near
content:
Republican President Donald Trump and Democratic former President Barack Obama were the most visible figures on the campaign trail this Wednesday, trading barbs even though neither is on the ballot. Their appearances came less than a week before the congressional elections that could shift Washington’s balance of power.

Thirty‑five of the 100 Senate seats and all 435 House seats will be contested next Tuesday. Nonpartisan analysts generally favor Democrats’ chances of capturing a majority in the House, while the Senate race is viewed as very close.
summary: Republican President Donald Trump and Democratic former President Barack Obama both campaigned on Wednesday despite not being on the ballot. With less than a week before the election, 35 Senate seats and all 435 House seats are contested, and analysts see a close Senate race and a Democratic advantage in the House.
author: France 24

title: Spain faces second deadly train crash of the year as election nears
content: A deadly train crash in Toledo province on Wednesday killed 69 people, marking the second fatal accident on the same line within nine months. The incident has been described as a serious blow to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s campaign ahead of the national election, with experts and the public accusing his government of underinvesting in railway infrastructure after years of rapid network expansion.
summary: The Wednesday crash in Toledo province killed 69 people. Occurring nine months after another fatal crash on the same line, it has intensified accusations of railway underinvestment under Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and dealt a blow to his election campaign.
author: France 24

title: Ship on fire in Strait of Hormuz as Iran says it shot down US drone
content: A British maritime agency reported that a ship in the Strait of Hormuz was on fire. At the same time, Iran said it had shot down another U.S. drone, noting that military tensions with Washington are ongoing.
summary: A British maritime agency reported that a ship in the Strait of Hormuz was on fire. Iran said it shot down another US drone amid ongoing military tensions with Washington.
author: DW World

title: ECB President Christine Lagarde to resign in February, nine months early
content: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announced she will resign in February, nine months before the scheduled conclusion of her eight‑year term. European Council President Antonio Costa said the search for her successor has already begun.
summary: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde will resign in February, nine months before the end of her eight-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa said the process to find a successor is underway.
author: DW World

title: India, EU deepen defense ties but clash on Russia, China, hindering maritime security
content: India and Europe are expanding their defence cooperation, yet divergent views on Russia and contrasting priorities regarding China are obstructing their shared goals for maritime security in the Indo‑Pacific region. These disagreements are limiting the ability of the EU and India to coordinate effectively on the area’s security agenda.
summary: India and Europe are deepening defense ties. However, their clashing perspectives on Russia and differing priorities on China are hampering their joint ambitions on maritime security.
author: DW World

title: Dozens of West Africans stranded in Guinea-Bissau after alleged trafficking
content: Dozens of West Africans who were drawn to Guinea‑Bissau by promises of employment and passage to Europe report exploitation by a suspected trafficking network. The victims now remain stranded in the country because they cannot afford to travel back home.
summary: Dozens of West Africans were lured to Guinea-Bissau with promises of jobs and migration to Europe and say they were exploited by a suspected trafficking network. Many now cannot afford to return home.
author: DW World

title: Security Council debates impact of drones and autonomous vessels on sea lane safety
content: At an open debate on Thursday, the Security Council examined how cheap drones, autonomous vessels and cyber‑attacks are reshaping threats to the world’s shipping lanes and the tools available to counter them. Delegates considered how emerging technologies could both endanger and protect seafarers, global trade and the flow of food and energy supplies.
summary: Cheap drones, autonomous vessels and cyberattacks are altering threats to the world’s shipping lanes. At an open debate on Thursday, the Security Council considered how emerging technologies could both endanger and protect seafarers, global trade and food and energy supplies.
author: UN News

title: Spain declares three days of mourning after high‑speed rail collision kills 69
content:
Spain has declared a three‑day period of mourning after a high‑speed rail collision claimed 69 lives. Emergency services, drones and a police dog unit are continuing to search the wreckage, while the Civil Guard has established clinics where relatives can provide DNA samples.

The accident involved two trains traveling on the same line from Madrid toward Andalucía. One was operated by the state‑owned Renfe and the other by the private company Iryo. Shortly before 9 a.m., the Iryo train stopped near the town of Urda in Castilla‑La Mancha, and the Renfe train struck its rear, knocking several carriages off the track.

Hospitals are treating dozens of injured passengers as families await news about their loved ones. The search and identification effort remains ongoing.
summary: Spain declares three days of mourning after high‑speed rail collision kills 69.
author: Guardian World

title: Finland and Norway leaders' 90‑minute call with Putin draws rebuke from Denmark, Sweden
content: With no single European representative negotiating directly with Moscow, some leaders are establishing their own channels – with messy results The Nordic countries rarely fall out in public over foreign policy, least of all over Russia. But a 90-minute phone call this week to Vladimir Putin by the leaders of Finland and Norway drew an unusual rebuke from their Danish and Swedish neighbours.
summary: With no single European representative negotiating directly with Moscow, some leaders are establishing their own channels. The leaders of Finland and Norway held a 90‑minute phone call with Vladimir Putin that drew an unusual rebuke from their Danish and Swedish neighbours.
author: Guardian World

title: Spain high‑speed train crash near Toledo kills at least 69, investigators probe signalling
content:
At least 69 people died when a high‑speed Renfe AVE train traveling from Madrid to Seville collided with an Iryo train on the same track near Toledo on Wednesday morning. Both trains had been stopped earlier after a signalling system failure; controllers later instructed the AVE driver to restart the journey, after which the AVE train struck the Iryo train from behind. The impact destroyed the AVE’s front carriages and the Iryo train’s rear, and caused additional derailing.

Investigators will examine the audio file that appears to implicate the control centre, as well as the signalling failure and other technical issues surrounding the restart order. Their inquiry will focus on why the AVE driver was told to proceed and how the signalling system malfunction contributed to the crash.
summary: At least 69 people died when a state‑owned Renfe AVE train from Madrid to Seville collided with a private Iryo train on the same track near Toledo on Wednesday morning after both were halted by a signalling failure. Investigators will question the control centre’s restart order, the signalling system and possible technical problems.
author: Guardian World

title: Rare letters from La Pérouse expedition reveal Louis XVI's 1793 inquiry about missing navigator
content:
A recent discovery of a “miracle” cache of letters written by a French scientist who perished in the ill‑fated La Pérouse mission has provided a personal account of the 1785 round‑the‑world voyage. The letters, now preserved, offer firsthand details of the expedition’s scientific objectives and daily life aboard the ships that were sent to rival the discoveries of English explorer Captain James Cook.

In the same historical context, the French king, Louis XVI, is reported to have asked, “Is there news of Monsieur de la Pérouse?” as he prepared to climb the scaffolding for his public execution by guillotine on 21 January 1793. The question referred to Jean‑François de Galaup, the Count of Pérouse, a naval officer and navigator who had been dispatched in 1785 on a global scientific mission.
summary: Rare letters from La Pérouse expedition reveal Louis XVI's 1793 inquiry about missing navigator.
author: Guardian World

title: Lawyers for Marist Brothers subpoenaed over advice to keep child abuser out of legal arena
content: A once-confidential letter says child sexual abuser might implicate senior church officials if allowed near ‘the legal arena’ upon his release from jail Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Lawyers from a leading law firm for the Marist Brothers have been subpoenaed to explain a once-confidential document showing they advised the Catholic order to keep a serial offender out of “the legal arena”, suggesting he was too honest and might implicate senior church officials. The offender was “regrettably up front” about his interactions with senior leadership, and could not be trusted to heed “suggestions” about “not dumping on others excessively”, the document says.
summary: Lawyers from a leading law firm representing the Marist Brothers were subpoenaed to explain a once‑confidential document. The document advised the Catholic order to keep a serial child sexual abuser out of “the legal arena” because he might implicate senior church officials.
author: Guardian World

title: Erin Patterson's appeal decision to determine possible retrial or longer sentence
content:
Erin Patterson will learn on Friday whether the Victorian Court of Appeal will impose a longer prison term or order a new trial in her triple‑murder case. The court, Victoria’s highest appellate body, is scheduled to deliver its ruling from 10 a.m. after hearing the two appeals.

Justices Lesley Taylor, Stephen McLeish and Peter Kidd heard arguments from Patterson’s legal team and prosecutors in August and will now determine the outcome of the appeals. The decision will address whether Patterson faces a retrial, a longer sentence, or both.
summary: Victoria’s Court of Appeal will deliver its decision on Friday on two appeals in Erin Patterson’s triple‑murder case, determining whether she faces a longer prison term or a new trial. The panel of Justices Lesley Taylor, Stephen McLeish and Peter Kidd heard arguments from her lawyers and prosecutors in August.
author: Guardian World

title: Study of 100,000 Australians seeks causes of mental health disorders and early onset cancer
content:
The Sax Institute has launched the 18 and Up study, an intergenerational research project that will follow the health of Australians aged 18 to 45 over the course of their lives. The independent, not‑for‑profit institute is recruiting 100,000 participants to become part of Australia’s largest study of wellbeing and ageing.

Researchers hope the data will help identify the drivers of major health challenges that affect younger people, including mental illness and rising cancer rates. By tracking participants over time, the study aims to uncover early risk factors and improve prevention strategies for mental health disorders and early‑onset cancer.
summary: Study of 100,000 Australians seeks causes of mental health disorders and early onset cancer.
author: Guardian World

title: Stephen Graham stars as serial killer Jurek Walter in new thriller Nocturne
content:
Stephen Graham stars as Jurek Walter, a sadistic serial killer, in the new 10-part psychological thriller Nocturne. The character is incarcerated for life in the basement of the Riverside psychiatric hospital in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Walter is depicted as a murderer who tortures both his victims and their families, utilizing a high-pitched giggle and fatal whispers to drive fellow inmates to suicide by communicating through the pipes. The review notes that Graham, described as muscle-bound and preternaturally still, delivers a mesmerizing and terrifying performance.

The article suggests that Graham may have surpassed Anthony Hopkins as the screen’s most profoundly unsettling serial killer, a status previously held by the actor from Hannibal. Walter is shown passing his time in confinement by doing push-ups and stashing contraband behind his toilet bowl for unspecified purposes. The review characterizes the series as a perfectly terrifying show suitable for Halloween, highlighting the difficulty of looking away from Graham’s portrayal of the character.
summary: Stephen Graham plays Jurek Walter, a sadistic murderer incarcerated at Riverside psychiatric hospital in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The character manipulates fellow inmates and tortures victims' families in the new 10-part psychological thriller.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Documentary explores Sylvester Stallone's creation of Rocky
content:
To mark the fiftieth anniversary of Rocky, a new film explores the life of Sylvester Stallone, highlighting his personal struggles before the movie’s release. The article notes that Stallone was belittled for his speech and appearance and was so financially strained that he sold his dog. Despite these hardships, he wrote and starred in the boxing film, which depicts a Philadelphia underdog who fights the world heavyweight champion to the final bell.

The creation of the film is described as an underdog story in itself, as the out-of-work character actor convinced a studio to finance the project and cast him in the title role. Stallone surpassed his fictional character by winning the best picture Oscar. The text emphasizes the enduring impact of the franchise, noting that thousands of people still climb the 72 steps of the Philadelphia Museum of Art annually to pay homage to the character.
summary: The article discusses how out-of-work actor Sylvester Stallone wrote and starred in the 1976 film Rocky. It highlights the movie's status as an underdog story that won a best picture Oscar and remains a cultural landmark.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Writers face surge in fake literary scams targeting aspiring authors
content:
Writers are increasingly targeted by a surge in literary scams, receiving daily invitations from fake book groups and offers to publicize their work. The article highlights how aspiring authors are often vulnerable to these fraudulent schemes. One specific example involves author Snigdha Poonam, who received an email from a man claiming to be Timothy Firth, the organizer of a Seattle-based life-drawing community called CAM Life Drawing.

The email addressed Poonam as “Professor” and claimed the group wanted to discuss her book, Dreamers: How Young Indians Are Changing Their World, at an upcoming meetup. Attendees were reportedly encouraged to leave reviews on Goodreads and Amazon afterward. Although Poonam found an events page and an Instagram account for the group, which featured photos and testimonials of a white male named Timothy Firth, she suspected the sender was not the genuine organizer. The piece questions who is behind this explosion in literary fraud.
summary: Writers are increasingly receiving daily invitations from fake book groups and offers to publicise their work. The article details a specific scam involving a fake organizer named Timothy Firth who contacted an author to discuss her book.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Mid-century modern furniture loses favor with millennials, says Norfolk dealer
content: Once coveted for its clean lines and timeless design, the functional furniture is no longer seen as cool. Anyone for cottagecore and chrome? “I definitely don’t think it is cringe,” says Laura Budds, a vintage furniture dealer based in Norfolk. “But I do think we have reached the peak, and we’re on the descent.” Budds is talking about mid-century modern furniture, which has recently come under fire from younger generations for being – like so many things, including trainer socks and high-waisted jeans – a deeply millennial aesthetic. As the Wall Street Journal declared : “Midcentury modern design has met the fate of pumpkin spice lattes, cocktails in mason jars, no-show socks, leggings and other aspects of millennial culture: it has become cringey.” Budds, 44, is resigned to the fact that she is a “mid-century millennial”. She’s even made a career out of it: she sells furniture and vintage clothes at Williams & Parfitt, a modern antiques centre in Wymondham, Norfolk. But she says she has had to diversify in recent years to cater to changing tastes among younger customers, who are moving away from the “wall-to-wall mid-century” look beloved by the generation above them. She says of gen Z: “I don’t think they are so bound by the eras or designers – they just buy what they like. They aren’t afraid of older antiques and will have a bit of whimsy or taxidermy.”
summary: Laura Budds, a 44‑year‑old vintage furniture dealer in Norfolk, says mid‑century modern furniture has peaked and is now viewed as cringey by younger generations. She has diversified her offerings at Williams & Parfitt in Wymondham as Gen Z shoppers move away from the “wall‑to‑wall mid‑century” look.
author: Guardian Culture

title: A three-year-old soccer prodigy went viral. The adults have already let him down
content:
A three-year-old boy from Florida gained significant attention after a video of his soccer skills went viral. In the footage, the toddler is shown running end-to-end and scoring multiple goals against opponents who appear to be just learning the game. The child’s father, identified as the cameraman, is seen loudly cheering his son on during the match. The story also involves a claim by the parents that police were called to the scene to stop opposing defenders who could not tackle the child.

Police records reviewed by the Guardian have complicated this narrative, raising troubling questions about the situation. The article notes that the internet broadly embraced the toddler, with references to figures like Ms. Rachel and Roc Nation. However, the piece argues that the actual tragedy is broader than the initial outrage cycle suggests, implicating more people and presenting a more depressing reality than the viral moment implies.
summary: A three-year-old soccer prodigy went viral. The adults have already let him down.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Tottenham's 2-0 win at Chelsea ends 34-match Premier League winless streak
content:
Tottenham Hotspur’s Premier League campaign has gained momentum following a 2-0 victory over Chelsea last Saturday. This result provided a significant boost to their standing in the table, marking a notable turnaround from their poor start to the season. The win is considered particularly substantial because it was a clean sheet at Stamford Bridge, a feat Tottenham had not achieved in any competition since December 1986.

The victory also broke a long-standing historical trend. Prior to this match, Tottenham had won only once in their previous 34 visits to Chelsea in the Premier League. That last win occurred in April 2018 under manager Mauricio Pochettino, a period when the team was described as a formidable force. For many supporters, this recent success represents a rare occurrence that has only been witnessed once before in their recent memory.
summary: Tottenham secured their first Premier League victory at Chelsea in 34 attempts with a 2-0 win. This result was also their first clean sheet at Stamford Bridge in any competition since December 1986.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Milwaukee Brewers close out Tampa Bay Rays to end 57-year wait for first World Series title
content:
The Milwaukee Brewers secured their first World Series title on Wednesday by defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5, completing a four-games-to-one victory. This championship ends a 57-year wait for the franchise’s first baseball prize. Rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt contributed two runs batted in, while Jacob Misiorowski pitched five and two-thirds scoreless innings in the decisive game.

Miguel Contreras was named the World Series MVP after batting .381 during the series. The victory marks the culmination of a season that began in spring training with championship ambitions, resulting in the first title in the franchise’s 58th year.
summary: Milwaukee Brewers close out Tampa Bay Rays to end 57-year wait for first World Series title.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Everton face Newcastle in Carabao Cup as owners seek sale
content:
Everton manager David Moyes faces a challenging backdrop as his team prepares for a Carabao Cup fourth-round match against Newcastle United at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The club’s owners, The Friedkin Group, have halted squad investment and announced plans to sell the team, a shift that contrasts with the season’s initial goals of European qualification and ending a trophy drought. Despite these changes in ownership direction and reduced resources, the demands on Moyes remain unchanged as he seeks to maintain the team’s competitive standards.

The upcoming match offers a specific opportunity for Everton to advance in a competition they have never won, potentially fulfilling one of their stated campaign objectives. The game is also seen as a chance to restore team morale following consecutive defeats against Chelsea and Arsenal, which are the only losses Everton has recorded this season. Newcastle fans will be present in significant numbers, with 7,732 supporters attending after Everton allocated 15% of the stadium capacity to their opponents.
summary: The Friedkin Group announced they are looking to sell Everton and have stopped squad investment, yet David Moyes must still pursue a trophy drought that will soon reach 32 years. Everton plays Newcastle in the Carabao Cup fourth round to restore positivity after consecutive defeats against Chelsea and Arsenal.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sri Lanka v England: Men's Cricket Tri-Series One-Day International Live
content: England began their final group match of the men’s cricket tri-series in Lahore against Sri Lanka, with the first over recorded at 0-0. Banton and Duckett were on strike as Asitha Fernando delivered the opening ball, which Banton nearly edged to slip. The venue featured empty green seats as the call to prayer rang out, marking the start of the day’s play.
summary: England began their final group match in Lahore with a score of 0-0. Asitha Fernando bowled the first over, which was a maiden.
author: Guardian Sport

title: ‘I’m no special guy. We can all do this’: Loek Hartog on rescuing Ollie Millroy from a burning car
content: Last month in Shanghai, the Dutch driver saved Ollie Millroy’s life after a crash. The incident created a unique friendship and a shared determination to improve safety Winter is coming and, at eight in the morning, Amsterdam is dark as Loek Hartog and I walk towards the park. The GT motor racing driver is only 24 but, after all he did last month, when he showed extraordinary courage in saving the life of his fellow racer Ollie Millroy, we talk easily about life and death. Hartog sips a takeaway coffee and, as we stroll, he asks if the world seems to be in a worse state than usual. Paris is burning, Kyiv is reeling, Vladimir Putin is being hailed as “a humanitarian” by Donald Trump’s envoy and the robots are coming for us. These are grim times, but I remind Hartog that he gave us hope as, after ripping off the doors of Millroy’s burning car as if he had stepped out of a superhero movie, his humanity was remarkably moving. Hartog dragged Millroy to safety before trying to comfort the 36-year-old Briton after an accident that left him with six broken ribs, a damaged lung, a splintered collarbone, a broken hand, a fractured C6 neck vertebrae and a stunned sense that he had almost died at the China GT.
summary: Last month in Shanghai, the Dutch driver saved Ollie Millroy’s life after a crash. The incident created a unique friendship and a shared determination to improve safety Winter is coming and, at eight in the morning, Amsterdam is dark as Loek Hartog and I walk towards the park.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pat Lam says Saracens did everything possible for Auvaa
content: Bristol Bears director of rugby Pat Lam tells BBC Radio Bristol Saracens did everything they could for Totoa Auvaa before he was sacked by them.
summary: Bristol Bears director of rugby Pat Lam stated that Saracens did everything they could for Totoa Auvaa. Lam made these comments to BBC Radio Bristol after Auvaa was sacked by Saracens.

title: Is Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho misunderstood after Barcelona win?
content: Jose Mourinho has observed other managers being celebrated as geniuses over the past decade. Following Real Madrid's recent victory at Barcelona, questions have arisen regarding whether the Real Madrid boss has been misunderstood in his reputation.
summary: Jose Mourinho has spent the past decade watching other managers be hailed as geniuses. A recent win by Real Madrid at Barcelona may suggest that he has been misunderstood.

content: The Milwaukee Brewers secured their first World Series championship in the franchise's 57-year history. The team defeated the Tampa Bay Rays in game five on Wednesday to claim the title.

title: DDoSecrets Publishes Data on 40,000+ DHS Employees
content:
Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets) released a dataset on Wednesday that lists more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including some who work in the intelligence community.  

The collective did not name the source of the personnel information; instead, it referred to the unnamed individual as the “Department of Peace.”
summary: DDoSecrets released a dataset containing information on over 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including some intelligence community staff. The leaker was unnamed and referred to as the “Department of Peace.”
author: The Hill

title: Crowley Holds 7-Point Lead Over Tiffany in Wisconsin Gubernatorial Poll
content: A new Marquette University Law School Poll released Wednesday shows Democrat David Crowley leading Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany (R‑Wis.) by 51 percent to 44 percent of likely Wisconsin voters, a 7‑point margin that represents a 2‑point increase from last month’s poll. The results indicate Crowley has slightly widened his advantage in the state’s gubernatorial race.
summary: Democrat David Crowley has slightly widened his lead over his GOP opponent, Rep. Tom Tiffany (R-Wis.), in Wisconsin’s gubernatorial contest, according to new polling released Wednesday.
author: The Hill
